To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed an adiabatic spin‐lock imaging sequence that allows for T1ρ imaging at 7 T and that we successfully applied it to the detection of dynamic glucose enhanced MRI (DGE‐MRI) in a rat model.
adiabatically‐prepared T1ρ‐weighted MRI can be applied to dynamic imaging of D‐glucose uptake in vivo at ultrahigh magnetic field strengths.

we developed a novel adiabatically‐prepared T1ρ‐weighted imaging sequence, that we demonstrated the feasibility of the method in vivo, and that we showed that the sequence is applicable to the detection of tumor‐to‐muscle ratios in patients with brain tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a T1ρ‐weighted imaging sequence for dynamic glucose enhanced MRI in vivo, the evaluation of the sensitivity of this sequence with respect to the administered dose, and its application to tumor patients at 7T.
the development of an imaging sequence for dynamic glucose enhanced (DGE) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at ultrahigh magnetic field strengths.
the development of an imaging method for the investigation of the uptake of D‐glucose into tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

adiabatically‐prepared spin‐lock experiments are an attractive alternative for T1ρ imaging in clinical studies at ultrahigh‐field whole‐body scanners, because of their insensitivity to RF field inhomogeneities and their potential for high‐resolution imaging.
the adiabatic spin‐lock technique is a robust and efficient approach for the investigation of glucose uptake at ultrahigh magnetic field strengths.
the adiabatically‐prepared T1ρ‐sequence can be used for in‐vivo dynamic studies of glucose uptake at ultrahigh‐fields and that the sequence is robust and reliable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adiabatic RF pulses allow to perform T1ρ‐weighted dynamic contrast‐enhanced MRI at 7T, and the method is applicable to clinical studies of glucose metabolism.
we were able to develop and validate an imaging sequence that allows the detection of glucose uptake in tumors in vivo at 7T.
we developed an adiabatic preparation for the T1ρ sequence that is robust against inhomogeneities of the RF field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T1ρ‐sequence can be used for D‐glucose enhanced MRI at ultrashort echo times (TE) at ultrahigh magnetic fields, and that this approach is robust against RF inhomogeneities.
adiabatically pre‐polarized spin locks can be used for dynamic glucose enhanced (DGE) MRI at ultrahight fields.
adiabatic RF pulses allow to perform T1ρ‐imaging at ultrahigh magnetic field strengths, which can be used for dynamic imaging of glucose uptake in tumors.
